blocks.heading: Accounting for planning and control
blocks.text: The accounting function records, organises and reports financial information. Planning uses that information to set budgets, forecast cash needs and compare possible uses of resources. Control compares actual results with plans, identifies differences and helps managers investigate their causes. A cost overrun might reflect higher material prices, more output or waste; the figure alone does not reveal which. Accurate records let managers distinguish those explanations before changing prices, suppliers or work methods. Financial statements also communicate results and position to users outside management. Historical figures do not guarantee future performance, so forecasts must state assumptions. A budget is a planned figure, not an actual receipt or permission to ignore service quality. Accounting supports decisions by supplying relevant evidence; it does not make every management choice on its own.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Oshi Pots budgets N$8,000 for monthly clay purchases but spends N$10,000 while producing more pots than planned. The accountant should compare quantities and prices, not conclude that the N$2,000 increase is entirely waste. Management can revise buying and production plans after identifying the cause. The control loop is plan, record actual results, compare, investigate and act.
